articles.title: Bill Gates Foundation to shutdown in 2045; by that year it aims to help millions of Americans with a skill it donated $400 million for; but why some 'do not agree with this 'gift'
articles.summary: The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline
articles.body: The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline healthcare workers, and farmers worldwide. Of this $1 billion, the largest single share of that funding — 40 percent, or $400 million — is earmarked directly for education. The foundation plans to direct those resources toward AI-powered tutoring systems designed to personalize instruction in classrooms both across the United States and abroad.The $400 million investment marks a major financial bet on a technology that entered widespread commercial use only a few years ago. It fits within a broader US education framework the foundation introduced in July, which targets helping up to 10 million more Americans secure career-advancing credentials of value before the organization concludes its operations in 2045.The donation also lands amid an escalating debate over the efficacy of digital tools in primary and secondary education. As school districts worldwide weigh classroom screen time, data privacy, and the measurable academic impact of recent tech adoptions, the foundation's venture signals a concerted effort to demonstrate that targeted, adaptive AI can deliver tangible outcomes rather than another cycle of tech-driven disruption.The skepticism is already shaping policy in some states in the US. Earlier this month, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced a moratorium on student-facing generative AI. Mamdani and Schools Chancellor announced a moratorium on student-facing generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) use in schools, alongside a new screen time policy, a decision that will impact nearly 600,000 public school students, or two-thirds of the system’s total enrollment. The policy establishes a one-year moratorium, effective in the 2026-2027 school year, on student-facing generative AI for children in 2-K through 8th grade. It also introduces twice-yearly AI critical thinking modules for high schoolers, limited AI pilots for a small number of high school classrooms and age-appropriate screen time restrictions.What Bill Gates said on the donation“The Gates Foundation was created in part to address a basic market failure: the people with the greatest needs often have the least power to shape where innovation and investment go,” writes Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation, in the report. “Much of our work has been about closing that gap. AI presents the same challenge, only at much greater speed. Left to the market alone, the most capable tools will be built first for the people and institutions most able to pay for them—not necessarily for those who could benefit most.”Gates adds, “We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident.” He further writes, “[I]t requires a deliberate, specific commitment from government leaders and the companies developing the technology: to measure success not only by what AI can do for the most profitable users but by what it can do for the people who stand the most to gain.”Gates Foundation to shut down in 2045In May 2025, Bill Gates announced that Gates Foundation will close its operations. In a note on Gates Notes, he wrote, "That is why I have decided to give my money back to society much faster than I had originally planned. I will give away virtually all my wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next 20 years to the cause of saving and improving lives around the world. And on December 31, 2045, the foundation will close its doors permanently."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: LPU suspends classes for 10 days, postpones mid-term exams amid protests over 'rape-murder' claims
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: Punjab’s Lovely Professional University postponed its mid-term examinations until further notice to ensure the safety and well-being of all
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Punjab’s Lovely Professional University postponed its mid-term examinations until further notice to ensure the safety and well-being of all students amid ongoing violent protests over an alleged rape case.The university has also suspended regular classes for 10 days starting September 28, it said in a statement."Regular classes will remain suspended for a period of 10 days with effect from 28th Sept. 2026 (Monday). Mid-Term Examinations are postponed until further notice. The revised examination schedule will be communicated separately via UMS," LPU said."Students may, in consultation with their parents/guardians, travel to their hometowns during this 10-day period, if they wish to do so. Students who stay back are advised to stay inside their hostels/places of residence and avoid unnecessary movement or involvement in any unrest activities in the interest of their own safety," the university further stated.The administration also appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Meanwhile, Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka held both the Centre and the Punjab government responsible for inciting these riots."I believe both the Central government and the Punjab government have failed; it is their responsibility to intervene immediately. I directly hold both the Centre and the Punjab government responsible for inciting these riots... I appeal to both the students and the administration to sit down and bring the situation under control immediately... I feel that a proper investigation has not been conducted; everything is happening in a state of panic. Neither the administration nor the university authorities seem to have a grip on the situation, and the students' voices are not being heard. I believe they need to act sensibly—whether it is the students or the administration—and handle this matter responsibly...," he told ANI.Massive student protests erupted in Punjab’s Phagwara area early Sunday morning after news spread on social media regarding the alleged rape of a university student within the campus premises.According to police, the investigation to ascertain the facts of the incident is ongoing; police officials have not yet confirmed whether a student was raped within the university campus. articles.title: Netanyahu secretly visited UAE, met Emirati leader in Abu Dhabi: Israeli official
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, a senior Israeli official told
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met UAE President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Sunday, a senior Israeli official told news agency Reuters, as the two countries navigate a sensitive regional security environment.However, neither Netanyahu’s office nor the UAE foreign ministry immediately issued a public statement on the meeting.The visit comes amid renewed attention in Israel to claims that the UAE leader had warned Netanyahu shortly before Hamas’ October 7, 2023 attack that the group was preparing a major operation.Dispute over reported warningIsraeli newspaper Haaretz reported earlier this month that Sheikh Mohammed had raised the warning with Netanyahu around a week and a half before the Hamas attack. The report said the information was not subsequently passed to Israeli intelligence agencies or the military.Netanyahu has rejected the report and threatened legal action against the newspaper. The issue has become politically sensitive as Netanyahu faces a difficult reelection campaign, with opposition figures accusing him of responsibility for security failures before the October 7 attack.The UAE has not commented directly on the Haaretz report. It has previously said that the two countries have maintained "open and direct lines of communication" since establishing diplomatic relations in 2020.A UAE source previously told Reuters that security issues are discussed with other countries through the "relevant entities", rather than "at the level of national leaders."UAE-Israel ties under scrutinyEarlier this year, the UAE denied that Sheikh Mohammed had met Netanyahu after the Israeli prime minister's office said in May that Netanyahu had "secretly visited" the Gulf country. A person familiar with the meeting later said the two leaders had met in Al-Ain, an oasis city in Abu Dhabi near the border with Oman, on March 26.The UAE and Israel established diplomatic relations under the Abraham Accords in 2020, making the Emirates one of the first Arab states to formally establish ties with Israel.Since coming under attack during the Iran war, the UAE has sought to strengthen its relationships with both Washington and Jerusalem. Its ties with Israel provide Abu Dhabi with a channel for regional engagement as well as closer access to the United States.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: ‘We will die’: Oleshky civilians eat weed to survive in Russian-held Ukrainian city
articles.summary: Ukraine’s Russian-occupied city of Oleshky is facing starvation, with around 2,000 civilians, including nearly 50 children, reportedly stranded as food
articles.body: Ukraine’s Russian-occupied city of Oleshky is facing starvation, with around 2,000 civilians, including nearly 50 children, reportedly stranded as food supplies run out and evacuation efforts remain stalled, The Guardian reported.A woman trapped in the city told The Guardian that she had lost more than 40kg since the war began and was struggling to find enough food. “Right now, I’ve got absolutely nothing to eat,” she said, adding that the home where she spent last winter had been destroyed and burned.Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson, has been described by Ukrainians familiar with the situation as a “hell on earth”.Residents survive on one meal a dayFood supplies to Oleshky reportedly began drying up after May as Russian forces expanded minefields and drone coverage around the city, making deliveries increasingly difficult.Residents told The Guardian they were sometimes surviving on just one meal a day — soup without potatoes, made from courgettes grown in former apartment flower boxes, and occasionally supplemented with foraged purslane, an edible weed.Four tonnes of aid dropped by dronesKherson’s military authorities carried out a large-scale drone operation over the weekend, dropping emergency food, water and medical supplies across Oleshky and nearby villages.According to the Kherson military governor’s office, about four tonnes of food were dropped at 100 locations. However, it remained unclear how much of the aid was intercepted by Russian forces.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha raised the situation in Oleshky at the UN General Assembly this week, warning of a “humanitarian catastrophe” and calling for the immediate evacuation of civilians.A food convoy heading towards Oleshky on September 1 was attacked, with Moscow blaming Ukrainian forces and Kyiv blaming Russian troops.You use AI every day. articles.title: Hotter seas, vanishing kelp, booming octopus: How Europe's marine life is changing
articles.summary: With European waters recording their hottest summer on record, rising ocean temperatures are affecting marine life across the continent, damaging habitats
articles.body: With European waters recording their hottest summer on record, rising ocean temperatures are affecting marine life across the continent, damaging habitats and forcing several species into new waters.According to a Reuters analysis, European waters averaged 21.6°C between June and August, the highest summer average in a 45-year record dating back to 1982.The warming has been particularly pronounced in the Bay of Biscay, a part of the northeastern Atlantic Ocean along the western coasts of France and northern Spain, where average sea temperatures reached 21.4°C during the summer, more than 2.4°C above the 1991-2020 average.The region also recorded 186 marine heatwave days by the end of August, highlighting the prolonged nature of the unusually warm conditions.The prolonged warming is also affecting marine habitats. Along the coast of Asturias in northern Spain, large brown kelp forests have declined sharply, with marine ecologist Jose Manuel Rico Ordas estimating that around 95 percent of the kelp stands sampled since 2010 have disappeared, according to Reuters.The loss of kelp is significant because the underwater forests provide food and shelter for several marine species, including sea urchins, lobsters and crayfish.As waters warm, species that depend on cooler conditions can come under pressure, while warmer-water species are increasingly moving into areas where they were previously less common.One of the clearest examples is emerging in southern England, where common octopus populations have surged as waters warm. Octopus landings, which were below 30 tonnes a year before 2025, rose to around 2,600 tonnes in 2025 and have crossed 3,000 tonnes in 2026, according to figures cited by Reuters.The shift in marine life is also changing the catch for fishermen. While some are benefiting from the sudden rise in octopus, others are seeing traditional catches such as crab, lobster and scallops decline, showing how warmer waters are reshaping Europe's fisheries.In the Mediterranean, warmer conditions are helping non-native species expand into new areas, adding to existing pressures on native marine life and changing local food chains.Scientists say the changes are being driven by more frequent and intense marine heatwaves, which can affect the survival, reproduction and movement of marine species.As ocean temperatures continue to rise, species adapted to cooler waters may face increasing pressure, while warmer-water species can expand into new habitats.You use AI every day. articles.title: Man slapped by Delhi minister Parvesh Verma was out on bail in MCD worker abduction, assault case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The man who was slapped by Delhi PWD minister Parvesh Verma during a confrontation over a newly laid road in west Delhi's Vikaspuri on Sunday
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The man who was slapped by Delhi PWD minister Parvesh Verma during a confrontation over a newly laid road in west Delhi's Vikaspuri on Sunday was out on bail in a June case registered at Tilak Nagar police station over the alleged assault of an MCD sanitation worker.The man, identified as Sahib Singh in connection with Sunday's incident, had been arrested in the earlier case and is currently out on bail.According to the complaint in FIR, registered at Tilak Nagar police station on the complaint of MCD sanitation worker Dhan Bahadur, three-four boys allegedly assaulted him and forcibly took him away on a scooter.Bahadur alleged that the men assaulted him, forcibly made him sit on a scooter and took him away.He said the scooter eventually stopped near a corner of a street, allowing him to somehow free himself with the help of some people.Bahadur was subsequently taken to hospital for treatment.The earlier case has come into focus after Sunday's confrontation in Vikaspuri, where Singh was seen recording Verma during an inspection of the newly laid Vikaspuri Ring Road.AAP MLA Jarnail Singh and his supporters had arrived at the site and questioned the quality of the road. In a video of the incident, workers are seen peeling off a portion of the bitumen layer, with Jarnail alleging that it came off "like a carpet".Singh, who identified himself as the MLA's social media handler, was walking alongside Verma and recording the inspection on his phone. As Singh moved closer, Verma reached towards the phone before slapping him."Oye maar kaise raha hai?" a man can be heard saying in the video. Verma's security personnel subsequently moved him away.AAP protested against the incident and demanded Verma's arrest. Police detained AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar and other party workers during the protest.Verma later defended his actions and alleged that Jarnail Singh had been pressuring PWD engineers to arrange a commission from the contractor. He also alleged that AAP workers had abused his family and obstructed road construction work."When one of their workers started hurling abuses at my family, I reacted just as anyone would in the heat of the moment," Verma said.Verma further alleged that Jarnail Singh and his supporters had been visiting the road after it was laid and damaging it before recording videos alleging corruption.Jarnail Singh rejected the allegations and said he had gone to inspect the road after receiving complaints about its quality. He alleged that instead of taking action over the condition of the road, Verma slapped the person recording the inspection.Police said two complaints had been received in connection with Sunday's confrontation. One was filed by the private road contractor, alleging that Jarnail Singh demanded Rs 50 lakh and issued threats. The other was filed by Singh against Verma over the alleged assault.Police said the complaints were being investigated and no FIR had been registered in connection with Sunday's confrontation at that stage.The political row intensified after the incident, with AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal condemning the alleged assault and announcing that he would visit the road to inspect it. articles.title: 'Would like to buy some?': Trump offered Xi US weapons as Washington sought to downplay Taiwan arms sale
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump sought to downplay Washington's pending arms sale to Taiwan by telling Chinese President Xi Jinping that the US sells weapons to
articles.body: US President Donald Trump sought to downplay Washington's pending arms sale to Taiwan by telling Chinese President Xi Jinping that the US sells weapons to countries around the world, and even asking whether China would like to buy some, according to US ambassador to China David Perdue.“President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point,” Perdue told Fox News on Sunday.Perdue made the remarks days after Trump hosted Xi for a state visit in Washington. He did not specify when Trump made the comment or provide further details about the exchange.Perdue was speaking about US policy toward Taiwan, which has been waiting for months for Trump to approve a new arms package worth about $14 billion.Fox News host Shannon Bream had raised concerns from Republican and Democratic lawmakers about delays in US weapons orders and aid packages for Taiwan, which is seeking to strengthen its defences against a potential Chinese attack.Bream asked whether Washington was holding back arms sales to Taiwan to avoid angering Xi. Perdue rejected that suggestion, saying Trump “is as strong on Taiwan as I've ever seen anybody” and has already approved substantial weapons sales to the island.Earlier, Trump also sought to play down Taiwan as a major point of friction with Beijing, saying the issue did not feature prominently in his latest talks with Xi.“We didn't talk about Taiwan too much with Xi. Right now, it's, you know, fine. It's just moving along. Xi understands very much how I feel,” Trump told reporters.Trump and Xi met at the White House last week as Washington and Beijing sought to stabilise ties following months of tensions over trade, technology and other geopolitical issues.The summit resulted in an extension of the US-China trade truce, while differences over Taiwan, artificial intelligence and Iran remained.Taiwan arms package remains pendingTaiwan has been waiting for months for Washington to approve a proposed arms package worth about $14 billion, following an $11 billion weapons deal announced last December.The latest package was put on hold after Trump’s meeting with Xi in Beijing in May. Trump has not indicated whether the deal will move forward following their latest summit.He had previously described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” in dealings with China.Beijing has repeatedly urged Washington to halt arms sales to Taiwan, which China claims as part of its territory. Ahead of the latest summit, China had made clear that Taiwan remained a major issue in its talks with Washington.According to China’s official news agency Xinhua, Xi urged Trump to “prudently handle the Taiwan question” and called on Washington to oppose Taiwan independence. The White House did not immediately release its own account of the discussion on Taiwan.Earlier, Taiwan deputy foreign minister Chen Ming-chi said Washington “very much” understands the island’s defence requirements and the military pressure it faces from China.“Taiwan faces a severe situation in the Taiwan Strait. Even though China's economy is declining, it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under this context, the US very much understands our defence needs,” Chen said.“We do continuously communicate with them, and we believe the US understands the situation we face and our determination on defence investment completely,” he added.Chen also said Taiwan had repeatedly received assurances from Washington that its policy toward the island had not changed. Perdue separately told CNBC that there had been no change in Trump’s Taiwan policy, including on arms sales.US balancing ties with China & TaiwanUnder US law, Washington is required to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself. The US does not formally recognise Taiwan as an independent country but remains its main informal security partner and arms supplier.At the same time, successive US administrations have left unclear whether Washington would directly intervene militarily if China attacked Taiwan.Beijing considers Taiwan part of China and opposes US arms sales to the island. Taiwan rejects China’s sovereignty claims and maintains that its future can be decided only by its people.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 2,000 cops deployed, classes suspended for 10 days: Lovely Professional University protests spiral into violence - top developments
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive. Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.Police deploy over 2,000 personnelA large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace...,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.Clashes, arson and highway blockadeThe protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Rape case registered, SIT formedPolice said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU denies rape claim, releases students' videoLPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”Congress attacks Punjab governmentThe opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘We are being scapegoated’: Why refugees fear renewed anti-migrant violence in South Africa
articles.summary: A September 30 deadline declared by South Africa's March and March, an anti-immigration movement that has led anti-migrant protests across the country
articles.body: A September 30 deadline declared by South Africa's March and March, an anti-immigration movement that has led anti-migrant protests across the country this year, has renewed fears of violence among migrant communities.Refugees are also fearing fresh unrest as South Africa will hold local government elections on November 4, with migration emerging as an increasingly prominent political and social issue.“I am in hiding now because they say they are going to kill me for speaking about the rights of foreigners,” Al Jazeera quoted Bishop Raphael Bahebwa, a refugee from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), as saying.Bahebwa has lived in South Africa for 26 years and has witnessed repeated flare-ups of anti-foreigner sentiment. But he says this year feels “different.”“It has been very tough. Never before have I experienced something like this,” he added.According to Kafuti Muyumba, another refugee from the DRC, many members of the refugee community were “afraid” to return to neighbourhoods where they had built businesses and lives. Muyumba, a small business owner and representative of the refugee community, said tensions had left many "fearful" for their safety.“People are afraid. Even the police allow March and March violence. They came with sticks and say we are attacking them. This is not the first time we are experiencing xenophobia. In 2008 and then in 2015 we also experienced this,” Muyumba stated.In 2008, xenophobic violence spread through townships and informal settlements across South Africa, killing dozens of people and displacing thousands. Further outbreaks of violence against foreign nationals followed in subsequent years.'We’re not xenophobic; campaign is against undocumented migration'March and March has described its mobilisation as a "campaign against undocumented immigration, crime and deteriorating conditions in South African communities," while arguing that the South African government’s response to immigration enforcement has been “insufficient”.The group has called for undocumented foreigners to leave South Africa and warned of further demonstrations if its demands are not met.Its leaders have repeatedly rejected accusations that the campaign is xenophobic, insisting that its target is undocumented migration rather than foreign nationals generally.March and March maintains that its sole demand is for undocumented immigrants to leave South Africa and return to their home countries.How has the South African government respondedIn response to the ongoing protests, the South African government has intensified immigration enforcement.Between June 14 and August 20, authorities processed 86,596 foreign nationals for deportation and repatriation, according to the government’s Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration.Malawians made up the largest group, followed by Zimbabweans and Mozambicans.Government data indicates that 90% of those repatriated had entered South Africa illegally, while 95% were classified as having crossed the border outside official ports of entry.The government maintains that the operations form part of a broader effort to strengthen border management and enforce immigration law.At the same time, officials have repeatedly warned private groups against taking immigration enforcement into their own hands.March and March’s September 30 deadline has no legal authority. The government maintains that ordinary citizens cannot deport anyone from South Africa.However, deadlines do not need legal force to create fear, as was the case for an earlier deadline of June 30."They are scapegoating us as foreigners. It is not going to end on September 30. It has to do with the elections," Bahebwa said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 70% Swiss say no: Switzerland rejects push for tighter neutrality amid Russia tensions
articles.summary: Switzerland has voted against a proposal aimed at tightening the country's long-standing policy of neutrality, with 70 per cent of voters rejecting the
articles.body: Switzerland has voted against a proposal aimed at tightening the country's long-standing policy of neutrality, with 70 per cent of voters rejecting the measure in a nationwide referendum on Sunday.The proposal was backed by the right-wing Swiss People’s Party, whose supporters argued that Switzerland had moved too close to the European Union and Nato, particularly because of its response to Russia’s war in Ukraine.The measure was rejected by majorities in all 26 Swiss regions, according to final results released by the Swiss government.What the proposal sought to changeThe initiative would have restricted Switzerland from joining sanctions against other countries unless those measures had been imposed by the United Nations.That would have significantly affected Switzerland’s ability to impose sanctions independently. Russia, one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, has veto power over decisions by the council.The proposal also sought to limit Switzerland’s cooperation with military alliances. Switzerland is not a member of NATO, but it has worked with the alliance for around three decades.Under the proposed rules, cooperation with a military alliance would generally have been prohibited unless Switzerland itself faced a threat.Debate over Switzerland’s neutralitySupporters said the government had moved “dangerously close” to the EU and Nato and argued that this could weaken Switzerland’s security and ability to act independently.The proposal followed Switzerland’s decision to adopt EU sanctions against Russia after its invasion of Ukraine.Swiss neutrality has been part of the country’s constitutional framework since the 19th century, but there has been a long-running debate over what neutrality should mean in a changing security environment.Opponents of the proposal argued that the federal government already had enough flexibility to protect Switzerland’s interests and respond to security threats.Voters divided over securitySecurity concerns featured prominently on both sides of the referendum. Ruth Bolomey, a 65-year-old retiree originally from Hawaii, said she voted for the initiative.“I believe we need neutrality and should keep neutrality for security reasons — for the people.”New York native Jihad Azkoul, 78, voted against the proposal. He said his decision was influenced by concerns over how Switzerland would respond if Russia attacked.“the question of what happens if Russia attacks us — would we be, would we get protection from our neighbors?”The referendum was part of Switzerland’s latest round of votes on national and local issues. The country’s system of direct democracy allows citizens to vote several times a year on proposed changes to laws and government policy.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Parked BMW on highway catches fire; consumer court orders insurer to pay Rs 70 lakh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra state consumer commission has directed United India Insurance Company to pay Rs 70 lakh to a BMW owner whose car was destroyed
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra state consumer commission has directed United India Insurance Company to pay Rs 70 lakh to a BMW owner whose car was destroyed by fire after it was parked on the roadside following a late-night tyre puncture. The commission also awarded 7 percent annual interest from the date the claim was rejected, Rs 50,000 for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs. The order was passed on September 16, 2026.Why did the BMW owner approach the commission?According to the commission order, Ravikant S Patil had insured his BMW car with United India Insurance Company under a policy valid from December 22, 2011 to December 21, 2012. The car had an Insured Declared Value (IDV) of Rs 70 lakh and Patil had paid a premium of Rs 1,65,996.On the night of March 8, 2012, the BMW suffered a tyre puncture on a highway. Because it was late at night, the driver moved the car to the side of the road, locked it and returned to Solapur in another vehicle.The next morning, the car was found completely burnt. The incident was subsequently recorded by the local police and fire department.The insurer registered the claim as a major “total loss” case but later rejected it, citing condition 4 of the insurance policy. The insurer said the car had been left unattended on the road without proper precautions and that this amounted to a breach of the policy conditions.Patil challenged the rejection before the consumer commission. He argued that the car had been locked and parked safely because the puncture occurred late at night and that the fire was an unforeseen incident. He sought Rs 99 lakh along with 18 percent annual interest.The insurer alleged that the puncture was only a minor breakdown and not an accident. It argued that the complainant or his driver should have stayed with the car or moved it to a safer place such as a nearby village or dhaba.The insurer also questioned why the spare tyre was not used or why the car was not towed back to Solapur using the second vehicle that had arrived at the spot.It relied on condition 4 of the policy, which required the insured to take reasonable steps to safeguard the vehicle and prevent further loss. The insurer also pointed to Patil's statement to the police that the car had been left unattended overnight.The insurer further disputed the cause of the fire. It said the spot panchnama showed burnt grass around 50 metres away from the car and argued that the cause of the fire was suspicious.It further claimed that the car's value, after depreciation, could not be more than Rs 59 lakh and argued that the complaint should be dismissed.Why did the commission reject the insurer's argument?The bench of presiding member Poonam V Maharshi, and member Dr Nisha Amol Chavhan examined condition 4 of the policy and said it did not completely prohibit leaving a broken-down vehicle unattended. Instead, it required proper precautions to be taken to prevent further damage or loss.The commission said what amounts to a proper precaution has to be considered according to the circumstances of each case.It found that the driver had moved the BMW to the side of the road near Chacha Dhaba, rolled up the windows and securely locked the vehicle. The commission said these actions showed that reasonable precautions had been taken.The commission also considered the fact that the puncture happened late at night on a state highway and that no tyre repair facility or mechanic was available at that hour in Dhulkhed.“Seeking an alternative vehicle to safely return to Solapur, while leaving the locked car parked on the roadside, was a practical and necessary decision, not a negligent one,” the commission said.The commission rejected the insurer's argument that the driver should have remained inside the vehicle overnight to protect it.“We find this argument not only hyper-technical but fundamentally flawed and insensitive. A vehicle parked on the shoulder of a highway at night is highly vulnerable to high-speed collisions and criminal elements. The law does not and cannot compel an insured individual or their employee to jeopardize their physical safety or risk their life merely to guard a depreciating material asset,” the commission added.The commission also said there must be a direct connection between an alleged breach of a policy condition and the loss before an insurer can reject a claim on that ground.It noted that the exact origin of the fire remained undetermined in the police and fire department records. The insurer had not produced forensic evidence showing that leaving the car locked on the roadside caused the fire.The commission also rejected the argument that failure to change the tyre using the spare tyre justified rejection of the claim. It said the inability to change a tyre at night did not allow the insurer to reject a total-loss claim arising from a separate incident of fire.The commission concluded that there was no evidence of wilful wrongdoing, serious negligence or bad faith by the complainant. It held that the insurer's reliance on condition 4 to reject the claim amounted to deficiency in service.The insurer had argued that the BMW's value after depreciation was not more than Rs 59 lakh. The commission rejected this argument.It said that once the Insured Declared Value had been agreed upon and the premium had been charged on that basis, the IDV becomes the value applicable for settling a total-loss claim.“The opposite party cannot unilaterally depreciate the value at the time of claim settlement without a statutory basis. The IDV of Rs. 70,00,000/- must be honoured,” the bench concluded.What did the consumer commission order?The Maharashtra state consumer commission partly allowed the complaint and directed United India Insurance Company to:Pay Rs 70 lakh, the Insured Declared Value of the BMW.Pay 7 percent annual interest on Rs 70 lakh from November 23, 2012, the date the claim was rejected, until actual payment.Pay Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment.Pay Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.The commission said the insurer's rejection of the claim amounted to deficiency in service.

articles.title: Over 30 killed in 3 separate attacks overnight in South Africa shootings; manhunt launched
articles.summary: South Africa police have launched a manhunt after three separate shootings across the country left more than 30 people dead and several others injured
articles.body: South Africa police have launched a manhunt after three separate shootings across the country left more than 30 people dead and several others injured overnight, as authorities grapple with persistent violent crime.In the deadliest incident, 17 people were killed and 15 wounded after eight unidentified gunmen opened fire at a tavern in Wedela township in the West Rand District outside Johannesburg on Saturday evening, police said.According to police, patrons were drinking inside and outside the tavern when the suspects arrived and opened fire on those outside before entering the establishment and continuing to shoot.The attackers were allegedly armed with pistols and AK-47 rifles. Police said they also searched some patrons and took their mobile phones before fleeing in two unidentified vehicles, CNN reported.Police have launched a search for the suspects, but no arrests have been reported so far.Four killed in Khayelitsha shootingPolice were also investigating a quadruple murder following a shooting in Khayelitsha township in the Western Cape at around 7.15pm on Saturday.Three men with multiple gunshot wounds were found at the scene. Two victims were discovered inside a vehicle, while another was found beside it. All three were declared dead at the scene.A fourth victim, who had also suffered gunshot wounds, was taken to a medical facility but died upon arrival, police said.No suspect has been identified or arrested, and the motive remains unknown.10 killed at Western Cape entertainment venueIn a separate incident, 10 people were shot dead at an entertainment venue in Lwandle township in South Africa’s Western Cape province early Sunday, police said.Gunmen reportedly entered the venue and opened fire on patrons. Five people died at the scene, while five others succumbed to their injuries in hospital.The latest attacks come amid concerns over persistent violent crime in South Africa. Experts have said mass shootings are becoming increasingly common, particularly in poorer communities.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: America’s first new nuclear warhead in nearly four decades - all about W93
articles.summary: The United States is developing its first new nuclear warhead programme in nearly four decades.
articles.body: The United States is developing its first new nuclear warhead programme in nearly four decades. The new W93 warhead, paired with the Mk7 reentry body, is now moving into the next stage of development for the US Navy’s submarine launched ballistic missile force.The US Navy said on that the W93/Mk7 programme has entered the Engineering and Manufacturing Development phase after achieving Milestone B earlier this year.The Navy described it as the first US nuclear warhead and reentry system programme initiated in nearly four decades, marking a major step in the modernisation of the sea based leg of the US nuclear deterrent.Vice Admiral Douglas Williams, director of the Navy’s Portfolio Acquisition Executive Strategic Systems Programs, said the W93/Mk7 is intended to provide flexibility and adaptability for future warfighter requirements while supporting an uninterrupted at sea nuclear deterrent.The Navy said the programme has been advanced through cooperation between Strategic Systems Programs, the National Nuclear Security Administration and industry partners.The last new US nuclear warhead to enter the stockpile was the W88 in 1988. The warhead is deployed with the Navy’s Trident II D5 submarine launched ballistic missile system and has since undergone the W88 Alt 370 modernisation programme.What are is nuclear warhead and reentry vehicle?A nuclear warhead is the part of a missile that carries the nuclear explosive. It is the warhead that produces the nuclear explosion when it reaches its target.A reentry vehicle is the protective body around the warhead. A ballistic missile can travel outside the atmosphere before heading back towards Earth. During this return, it faces extremely high temperatures and pressure. The reentry vehicle protects the warhead during this stage and helps deliver it towards its target.In the W93/Mk7 programme, the W93 is the nuclear warhead, while the Mk7 is the reentry body that carries and protects it. The two are being developed together for the US Navy’s submarine launched ballistic missile force.How the W93 will be usedThe W93/Mk7 is being developed for the US Navy’s Trident II D5 submarine-launched ballistic missile system. The Trident II D5 currently carries the Navy’s W76 and W88 nuclear warheads, with the warheads housed inside reentry bodies.The Navy says the future D5 Life Extension 2 (D5LE2) system will incorporate the new W93/Mk7 alongside the existing W76 and W88 families.The missiles are currently deployed aboard the Navy’s 14 Ohio-class ballistic missile submarines. Each operational Ohio-class SSBN is limited to 20 Trident II D5 missiles, after four of its original 24 missile tubes were permanently deactivated.Each Trident II D5 is a multiple-warhead missile, meaning a single missile can release more than one independently targeted reentry vehicle.

articles.title: Tensions flare in Ujjain after group clashes with police over portion of Shahi mosque demolition
articles.summary: UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening
articles.body: UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project, news agency ANI reported on Monday.Heavy police force remains deployed in the area.The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.272 structures have been marked for demolitionEarlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.He added that the gesture was meant to set an example for residents whose properties were also being affected by the project."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation Chairperson Kalawati Yadav explained the scale of preparations underway for the upcoming religious gathering, as it is one of the biggest spiritual gatherings that happens once every 12 years."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. Extensive preparations are underway, including around 29 kilometres of new ghats, a diversion project, dams and other infrastructure works to improve the city. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening initiative forms part of the broader infrastructure overhaul being undertaken in Ujjain to accommodate the massive influx of pilgrims expected during the Simhastha Mela in 2028.(With inputs from ANI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Indore | Silver Rate in Indore | Bank Holidays in Indore | Public Holidays in Indore | Petrol Price in Indore | Diesel Price in Indore | CNG Price in Indore | LPG Price in IndoreStay updated with the latest Indore news. articles.title: Home & Decor Awards 2026: Celebrating the people and ideas shaping India’s spaces
articles.summary: What makes a house feel like home? Is it the architecture, the interiors, the furniture or the lighting? Or all these combined?
articles.body: What makes a house feel like home? Is it the architecture, the interiors, the furniture or the lighting? Or all these combined? As India’s homes and urban landscapes evolve, design is increasingly becoming about more than aesthetics, it is about functionality, innovation, sustainability and the way people experience the spaces around them.Times of IndiaHome & Decor Awards 2026Against this backdrop, the Times of India Home & Decor Awards 2026 brings together architects, interior designers, real estate professionals, home brands and creative voices to recognise excellence across the evolving world of homes and living spaces.Positioned by the organisers as a recognition platform celebrating design excellence across homes, spaces and modern living, the awards span 40 award categories and multiple special recognitions, covering everything from home automation and modular kitchens to architecture, real estate, luxury residences, furniture, art, lighting and sustainable homes.The juryThe jury brings together professionals from architecture, design, real estate and creative fields, including Raseel Gujral Ansal (India’s Leading Voices in Luxury Design), Komal Sanghavi Vasa (Founder - Gesamt Design), Anshuman Magazine (Chairman & CEO for India, South-East Asia, Middle East, and Africa at CBRE), Aparna Kaushik (Founder and Principal Architect), Ravi Kewalramani (Real Estate Entrepreneur and Digital Creator), Dr Gopalan Nair Shankar (People's Architect, Padmashree Awardee, Habitat Technology Group) and Sussanne Khan (Creative Director & Founder The Charcoal Project - Sussanne Khan House of Design).Where Art Meets DesignOne of the opening conversations, “Where Art Meets Design: Creating Spaces with Character,” will explore the relationship between art and interiors and how personal expression can give a space its identity.The award categories themselves reflect the breadth of India’s rapidly changing home and design ecosystem. Early categories include Baby Cot/Kids Living Solutions, Garden & Landscape Brand, Emerging Designer, Home Automation Brand, Best D2C Home Brand, Home Brand and Innovation in Living. Special recognitions will also acknowledge innovation in areas such as kitchen and wardrobe solutions, modular kitchens and bathware design.The Future of Real EstateReal estate and the built environment will form another important part of the evening. A conversation titled “The Future of Real Estate: Building for a New India”, featuring Anshuman Magazine and Ravi Kewalramani, will look at how the sector is responding to changing expectations around homes and urban development.Architecture takes centre stage in the first panel discussion, “The Future of Indian Architecture: Designing for People, Place & Progress.” The panel will discuss the relationship between architecture, people and the changing Indian context.The second half of the event moves into the details that complete a home, with awards recognising modular kitchens, kitchen appliances, sanitaryware, flooring, rugs and carpets, lighting, curtains and blinds, upholstery and furnishing fabrics. Another panel, “The Art of Choosing: Understanding Art for Your Space,” will explore how art can influence and complement residential interiors.The awardsThe final set of awards focuses on some of the most aspirational segments of the property and design landscape. These include Architect of the Year, Best Sustainable Home, Best Apartment Design, Best Themed Project of the Year, Real Estate Icon of the Year – Lifetime Achievement, Iconic Real Estate Project of the Year, Real Estate Entrepreneur of the Year, Interior Designer of the Year, Iconic Project of the Year, Best Luxury Residence, Luxury Villa Project of the Year and Ultra-Luxury Residential Project of the Year.Together, the categories offer a snapshot of how India's relationship with its homes is changing. From smart technology and sustainable construction to personalised interiors, luxury residences and innovative materials, the focus is increasingly on creating spaces that combine design with purpose.The Times of India Home & Decor Awards 2026 therefore aims to bring together multiple sides of the industry under one platform—recognising established names while also spotlighting emerging designers, innovative brands, distinctive projects and new approaches to modern living. articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns today
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns at the Government Rajaji
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns at the Government Rajaji Hospital in Madurai on Monday, fulfilling an electoral promise.The initiative, called the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting women’s health and encouraging institutional deliveries by attracting more families to government healthcare facilities.Vijay will present 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns during the statewide launch. The state government has allocated an annual budget of Rs 755.83 crore for the scheme.The scheme will cover eligible babies born on or after June 22, 2026, at government institutions to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will carry a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.Mothers will have to submit proof of residence to avail the benefit. Documents accepted include ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6.Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will oversee the scheme’s implementation and monitoring.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Blown them away with that whistle’: TVK takes swipe at Udhayanidhi over bypolls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Rocky Hill-Glastonbury Ferry continues its historic Connecticut River service, carrying three cars at a time on a crossing that dates to 1655
articles.summary: A ferry has crossed the Connecticut River between Rocky Hill and Glastonbury since 1655, when the service began with a small raft pushed across the river
articles.body: A ferry has crossed the Connecticut River between Rocky Hill and Glastonbury since 1655, when the service began with a small raft pushed across the river using long poles. Over the centuries, the ferry has changed from horse-powered and steam-driven vessels to its current operation. Today, the three-car Hollister III, an open flatboat, is towed across the river by the diesel-powered Cumberland. The Rocky Hill-Glastonbury Ferry operates from April through November, providing a direct river crossing for motorists, pedestrians and cyclists. According to the Connecticut Department of Transportation, it is the oldest continuously operational ferry in the United States.How the ferry changed from horsepower to a diesel towboatThe ferry has changed considerably since its early days. At one point, horses on treadmills in the centre of the craft provided the power needed to move it across the river. CTDOT's history of the ferry states that it was modernised in 1876, when the service moved to steam-driven craft.The ferry's current operation uses a different form of propulsion. CTDOT describes today's vessel as an open flatboat named the Hollister III, which can carry three cars. The barge is towed back and forth between the landings by Cumberland, a diesel-powered towboat.Rocky Hill-Glastonbury Ferry schedule and faresThe ferry normally operates from April 1 through November 30. CTDOT lists operating hours of 7 a.m. to 6:45 p.m. from Monday to Friday, and 10:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays and Sundays. The ferry is closed on Thanksgiving, and weather conditions, water levels or mechanical issues can affect service.The ferry operates on demand rather than according to fixed departure times. CTDOT states that there are "no scheduled departure times" and that service is provided as vehicles and passengers arrive. Vehicles can board for $5 on weekdays and $6 on weekends, while pedestrians and cyclists pay $2 on all days, according to the department's current ferry information.How the ferry saves drivers nearly eight milesThe ferry provides a direct connection between Rocky Hill and Glastonbury at Route 160. CTDOT says motorists travelling between parts of southern Glastonbury and Rocky Hill can cut nearly eight miles one way from their journey by using the ferry. The department also identifies the crossing as particularly important for cyclists.Cyclists cannot use the Putnam Bridge on Route 2 between Wethersfield and northern Glastonbury, according to CTDOT. The department's ferry history page states that the Rocky Hill-Glastonbury Ferry is the only crossing available to cyclists between Hartford and Middletown, leaving a barrier of more than 13 miles without the ferry. High water near the landings delayed the April 1 start; CTDOT announced a May 1 opening. It was expected to welcome passengers through November.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Why the PM could finally drop the triple lock pension pledge
articles.summary: Andy Burnham said that he would make tough decisions to fund a new national care service.
articles.body:
The prime minister's Sunday morning BBC interview set hares running when it comes to the future of a policy once seen as politically untouchable.

The timing of the PM's new social care plan sparked suggestions the government could be about to signal the death knell to the state pension triple lock after 16 years.

Andy Burnham said he will put forward tough decisions to fund a new national care service as part of Labour's next general election manifesto, seeking a mandate to make the changes next Parliament.

The triple lock, which in theory expires at the end of this Parliament, means state pensions rise every April by at least 2.5%, or in line with the highest of prices or earnings.

Earlier this month, BBC News put this precise question about changing the triple lock in the next Parliament to Chancellor John Healey, who replied "the PM has said, like I have, that we must bring down welfare costs".

It was a non-denial reflecting the fact that the PM has been besieged with advice, including from some of his favourite economists, that scrapping the triple lock, or even signalling it is a future possibility, is a golden opportunity for Britain's economic policy at a tricky moment in the bond markets for all heavily indebted nations.

The UK specifically is seen as a place where successive governments have shirked tough long-term decisions. Could this be Burnham and Healey's attempt to shift that perception, even in the slightly wild markets for government borrowing?

The politics are trickier. Reform's leaders see the policy as a key potential dividing line with Labour.

Many in Westminster privately agree the Osborne-era policy is unsustainable economically, but argue it is politically impossible to unpick.

Many pensions campaigners point to the fact that even after increases, the UK's state pension is not generous by international standards, though other countries have very different systems and rates of private provision.

Former ministers point out that the quid pro quo of redeploying the pension cash savings towards an in kind care service could shift the argument.

The lock is costing £15.5bn a year, treble original estimates of the 2030 cost, especially because of the volatility of prices and earnings.

Reverting to an earnings link could save tens of billions of pounds a year in the long run.

It is the sort of saving that could plausibly fund some form of national care service, potentially with cash left over as a buffer in a volatile world - but that depends on the ambition of the care plan, the generosity of any replacement for the triple lock, and how volatile prices are in the long term.

It had been deemed politically unthinkable, but the government now seems to be thinking about it, at least for the future.

articles.title: Dozens killed as monsoon wreaks havoc across India, Nepal and Thailand
articles.summary: A brutal monsoon season has swept across South and Southeast Asia, killing over 90 people across three countries and displacing hundreds of thousands.
articles.body: LUCKNOW, India — At least 62 people have died after days of heavy rain and flooding in northern India’s Uttar Pradesh state, officials said Monday. The state government said 46 people were injured and more than 1,000 houses were damaged after three days of heavy rainfall caused flooding in several districts. Schools were closed Monday in parts of the state, including the capital, Lucknow, while rescue teams moved people from flooded areas to safer locations. Residents were advised to avoid unnecessary travel through waterlogged areas and stay away from fast-flowing rivers, streams and drains. Rainfall was expected to ease from Monday as a weather system over the Bay of Bengal weakened, said Atul Kumar Singh, a senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow. Light rain could continue in eastern and western parts of the state through Tuesday, he said. Flooding also affected the eastern state of Odisha, where more than 75,000 people were evacuated to safer areas, officials said. In neighboring Nepal, 21 people died in weather-related incidents from Thursday through Sunday, the country’s disaster management agency said. Five people remained missing and five others were injured, while floods and landslides damaged 194 houses. Nepal is still recovering from devastating August floods that killed more than 1,400 people and left nearly 6,000 missing. Thousands sheltered on Monday in evacuation centres in the Thai capital, parts of it still flooded after havoc brought by intense weekend rain, while swelling reservoirs in an eastern province triggered orders for more to leave their homes. Entire neighborhoods were inundated and the drainage network swamped after over 12 inches of rain fell during two or three days last week, or nearly as much as the sprawling low-lying city usually gets in all of September. “Over 80,000 residents living in flooded areas are unable to leave their homes,” Unsit Sampuntharat, the permanent secretary of the interior ministry, said in a statement, adding that mobile kitchen and boats were being mobilized in relief efforts. “The goal is to provide three meals a day to all residents throughout the ... flooding period and for at least another seven after waters recede,” he added, amid intermittent showers on Monday. Bangkok is among 41 provinces across Thailand hit by floods since September 16 that killed at least eight people and disrupted more than 580,000 homes, the ministry said. The floods could cause economic damage of at least 11 billion baht ($327 million) nationwide, with the losses likely to rise unless the situation improves, said Aat Pisanwanich of Rangsit University’s economics department. “The flooding is expected to shave 0.3 percentage points off this year’s GDP growth, reducing growth to 2.1%, and cut third-quarter growth by about 0.5 percentage points to 1.7%,” he told Reuters. Southeast Asia’s second-largest economy, which has lagged regional peers since the COVID-19 pandemic, expanded 1.9% year-on-year in the year’s second quarter, but that was still down sharply from the previous quarter’s growth of 2.8%. Bangkok and the eastern region are likely to take the brunt of the impact, particularly wholesale and retail businesses, while industry and agriculture will suffer elsewhere, Aat added. Residents waded through waist-deep waters in the capital’s hard-hit neighbourhood of Bang Kapi to buy essentials from vendors, some of whom set up stalls with floating plastic boxes and drums, three days after incessant rain brought floods. At least 5,901 people in Bangkok have moved to 234 evacuation centres, a city administration official said. Sitting on a river delta of soft clay just 5 feet above sea level, heavily-built up Bangkok is sinking by several millimetres a year, while its population of more than 8.4 million often battles floods in its six-month-long rainy season. Further east, in the coastal province of Rayong abutting a major industrial belt, authorities ordered evacuations on Monday after flood waters swelled two reservoirs beyond their capacity. Last year’s catastrophic southern floods, triggered by 25 inches of rain over three days, killed at least 145, inundated more than 33,000 homes and damaged critical facilities such as schools, hospitals and highways.

articles.title: Indian university suspends classes amid violent protests over alleged rape
articles.summary: Lovely University suspends classes for 10 days due to campus unrest over rape allegations denied by officials.
articles.body:
A university in the Indian state of Punjab has suspended classes for 10 days after protests on campus over an alleged rape last week, a claim that university officials have denied.

In an announcement on Monday, Lovely Professional University in Phagwara also postponed midterm examinations due to the demonstrations, which turned violent.

“Students may, in consultation with their parents/guardians, travel to their hometowns during this 10-day period, if they wish to do so,” it said in a statement.

“Students who stay back are advised to stay inside their hostels/places of residence and avoid unnecessary movement or involvement in any unrest-related activities in the interest of their own safety.”

According to posts on social media, a female student was raped on campus. Some claimed the student committed suicide. Police said they were investigating the alleged incident, adding that the identity of the student had not been established, the news magazine India Today reported.

The protests escalated on Sunday as demonstrators clashed with police, and reports in local media said there were incidents of vandalism inside the university.

Protesters allegedly threw stones, smashed windows and set fire to vehicles on campus as well as damaging police vehicles, according to reports. Students also reportedly blocked a nearby highway.

University registrar Monica Gulati denied the rape had taken place, saying on Sunday that there was “no truth” to the allegations.

“The manner in which such false and misleading information is being systematically circulated appears to be a deliberate and concerted attempt to malign the reputation of the university and tarnish its image,” The Times of India, the country’s largest English newspaper, reported.

Meanwhile, three female students residing in the same building where the alleged rape took place appeared in a video featuring Gulati and backing the registrar’s claims that no rape had taken place.

However, according to the news channel NDTV, a separate video emerged later in which the same three students said they were instructed on what statements to make.

The incident comes as the Supreme Court on Monday ⁠⁠pushed for ⁠⁠accountability over a recent spate of rape cases in the national capital and neighbouring districts, saying ⁠⁠they reflected a “failure of law enforcement”.

Hundreds of students protested in Delhi ⁠⁠last week to demand better safety for women after a teenager said she was raped by three men at a park in the city.

Last month, a 17-year-old ‌‌girl was allegedly raped in a moving bus by the driver and conductor, local media reported.

Sexual violence ⁠⁠is a major problem across ⁠⁠India with more than 80 rapes reported to police every day, according to the National Crime Records Bureau. Activists said that number is a major undercount and many victims do not report rapes because of social stigma or coercion.

articles.title: Trump expects more talks after rejecting latest Iranian proposal
articles.summary: President Trump said Sunday he expects U.S. officials to negotiate further with their Iranian counterparts this week, after he rejected a seven-day ceasefire proposal from Tehran. “I expect more talks with Iran [this week]. They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make,” Trump told Axios in…
articles.body:
President Trump said Sunday he expects U.S. officials to negotiate further with their Iranian counterparts this week, after he rejected a seven-day ceasefire proposal from Tehran.

“I expect more talks with Iran [this week]. They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make,” Trump told Axios in a phone interview. “It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago. They overplayed their hand.”

The president added that he is “always thinking” about resuming strikes on Iran, as the war hits the seven-month mark on Monday.

Trump turned down a seven-day ceasefire proposal from Iranian officials, telling reporters on Saturday that negotiators from the Islamic Republic “want to make a deal where they open” the Strait of Hormuz “immediately.”

The Iranian military’s restrictions on shipping in the key waterway have rocked the global oil trade. Brent crude, the international benchmark, is trading at more than $107 per barrel as of Monday.

“They want to make a deal, and I think that’s fine, I like making a deal, too, but that deal would not be acceptable,” the president said Saturday of the Iranian proposal.

U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz backed Trump up on Sunday that the Iranians asked for “ everything up front ” as part of a short-term ceasefire.

Waltz, in an interview on CNN’s “State of the Union,” echoed the president in saying the Iranians are “miscalculating” Trump’s consideration of the midterm elections during the war. But Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that he and his fellow government officials “don’t care” about the U.S. election.

“We don’t care about any other things. We care about our national interests,” Araghchi told “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker on NBC. “We are ready to negotiate as much as we are ready to face any challenge.”

“We stand firm in the face of any aggression against us, even if it comes to a doomsday war,” he continued. “At the same time, we are ready for diplomacy.”
